note: This skill's output is an interactive multi-turn coaching conversation, so automated single-shot evals can only test the OPENING behavior (triage-first, tutor-not-narrator, no pack dump) and pack quality. Full evaluation needs a human-in-the-loop run of each phase, plus a delayed measure (can the user answer cold the next day?) — end-of-session satisfaction is confounded by the fluency illusion.

evals.prompt: You just finished writing a 12-slide investment proposal for me (recommending we spend £400k migrating our client portal to a new platform, paid back in 19 months through support-cost savings). I'm presenting it to our exec board on Thursday and the FD, Priya, is famously brutal on numbers. Brief me properly so I can defend it.
evals.expected_output: Opens with stakes triage (audience/exposure/stakes), declares Level 3, builds pack silently, then starts the BOT-LED guided walk-through (walk-check-correct-move), one question at a time — it must NOT open by asking the user to generate questions ('grill me, where do you want to start?'), and must NOT paste the full pack or a wall of content. Mentions voice option for the rehearsal phase.

evals.prompt: ok so chatgpt wrote this proposal for my client meeting tomorrow morning and honestly i don't understand half of it. they're going to grill me. help??
evals.expected_output: Recognizes entry mode B (content produced elsewhere): asks for the content and the original client brief/ask, triages stakes and time, flags that unverifiable claims will be marked rather than guessed. Reassuring but structured; one question at a time.

evals.prompt: I've read the strategy doc you wrote twice, I'm across it. Just give me a list of likely questions and model answers I can memorize tonight for the steering committee.
evals.expected_output: Declines the script request warmly with the first-follow-up rationale, offers frameworks + interactive Q&A instead, and deploys the 90-second bet (three closed-book questions) to calibrate. Does not just hand over a Q&A script.
